chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from his father, from ʿAlī ibn ʿUqbah and Dhubyān ibn Ḥakīm, from Mūsā ibn Ukayl al-Numayrī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding sprinkling water upon the grave is that he should face the qiblah, and begin from the side of the head to the side of the feet, then go around the grave from the other side, then sprinkle upon the middle of the grave; thus is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) concerning it.”

key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head side of the grave
key_terms.الرِّجْلِ: the foot side of the grave
key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the prescribed prophetic tradition or established normative practice
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer toward which one faces
key_terms.رَشِّ الْمَاءِ: sprinkling water in the funerary rite
key_terms.وَسَطِ الْقَبْرِ: the middle of the grave where the final sprinkling is done

ai.seo_question: What is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) method of sprinkling water on a grave in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the prescribed sunnah (prophetic tradition) manner for sprinkling water on a grave after burial. It describes the direction, starting point, path around the grave, and concluding sprinkle, indicating an established funerary practice in Shia jurisprudence.
